sourceReasons: P. 1 explicitly lists vegetation (green) among area features in this named USGS topographic-map brochure. This supports the scoped color/class association asked; it does not establish a convention for all maps.

fieldGroups.editorialReason: Two concise sentences name and explain the key, retain the source boundary and do not turn the brochure-specific legend into a universal rule.

sourceReasons: P. 1 identifies vegetation as a green area feature; the card itself explicitly limits the claim to this brochure and its topographic-map symbol system.

fieldGroups.editorialReason: Adds a concrete independent fact: four vegetation classes represented by green legend symbols. It supplements the prompt/key rather than repeating “vegetation is green”; 13 words, within the 35-word limit.
fieldGroups.literal: В легенде USGS зелёными знаками показаны лесные массивы, кустарники, сады и виноградники.
sourceReasons: P. 4 VEGETATION legend separately lists Woodland, Shrubland, Orchard and Vineyard, each with a green symbol swatch. Mangrove is listed separately with a mixed blue water/vegetation pattern, so the note carefully names only the four green-coded entries rather than claiming every vegetation symbol is green.

fieldGroups.editorialReason: Provides concrete water-feature examples for the blue distractor, not an unsupported claim that every water-related mark is blue.
fieldGroups.literal: Синим в брошюре обозначены водные объекты, включая озёра и ручьи.
sourceReasons: P. 1 names lakes, streams and irrigation ditches as hydrographic examples; p. 4 RIVERS, LAKES, AND CANALS visually labels stream/river/lake/canal symbol rows.

fieldGroups.editorialReason: Explains the brown-line distractor with the equal-elevation meaning; maintains the topographic-contour scope.
fieldGroups.literal: Горизонтали в брошюре показаны коричневыми линиями; каждая соединяет точки одинаковой высоты.
sourceReasons: P. 1 says topographic contours are brown and each contour is a line of equal elevation; p. 2 separates topographic contours from bathymetric contours.

fieldGroups.editorialReason: Gives concrete feature classes for the black-sign distractor, preserves “обычно” and “другие дороги” to avoid overstating the source.
fieldGroups.literal: Чёрным обычно показаны другие дороги и тропы, железные дороги, границы и другие культурные объекты.
sourceReasons: P. 1 says other roads and trails, railroads, boundaries and other cultural features are usually black, contrasting important roads in red; p. 4 road rows show multiple symbol variants.
